result.narrative:
Maasland Agro Processing BV scores 66.9 with a PD of 0.6396, placing it in the High Risk band. The driver is a single seriously overdue invoice: INV000340 at 55 days past due on 60-day terms, worth €140,000, sitting alongside €1.13M of other open invoices that are not yet due. Total open exposure with the one insurer on risk is €1,267,900 against a credit line of €1,380,000. Supporting this is one severity 4 news item from 334 days ago reporting a capacity cut at the Zwolle unit.

The band is built from 0.65 x 90.0 (payment, 55 DPD) + 0.35 x 23.9 (news) = 66.9. The adjudicator agreed with caveats and the caveats matter here. The payment raw of 90.0 is set by worst-line DPD alone and treats the whole €1,267,900 relationship as if it were 55 DPD, when only €140,000 is actually past due. There is no settled invoice history at all, so the payment agent recorded the trend as insufficient_history and no baseline exists to tell a structural problem from a one-off dispute. Most significantly, payment alone gives 58.5, below the 60.0 High Risk cutoff, so the 8.4 weighted points from a 334-day-old, largely single-sourced article are what carry this buyer from Watch into High Risk.

The recommendation is REDUCE on the one line: Solvenza Trade Credit (CL03) from €1,380,000 down to €1,267,900, which cuts expected loss from €637,713 to €585,911. This is a cut to current outstandings rather than a withdrawal, so it stops further drawdown without disturbing the existing book. Against that, the payment agent flags concentration risk not captured in the formula: only one insurer holds a line, and open exposure sits close to it.

Before treating the band as settled, the two things worth resolving are the status of INV000340 and whether the Zwolle capacity cut persisted. The score is 6.9 points above the Watch line at 60.0, and the news component decays on a 365-day half-life, so the band does not hold on news alone indefinitely.

judgement.bottom_line: Reduce the Solvenza Trade Credit line from €1,380,000 to €1,267,900, cutting exposure to current outstandings on a 55 DPD overdue and a PD of 0.6396. The adjudicator agreed only with caveats: payment alone scores 58.5, below the 60.0 cutoff, so the High Risk band rests entirely on one 334-day-old article.
